Plot the pathways whose history changes the prediction most

Source: R/plot_pathways.R
plot_divergence.Rd

plot_divergence() ranks pathways by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, in bits, between their next-state distribution and that of their shorter suffix, the context without the earliest state. In a variable-order model a longer history matters only where it changes what is expected next. Each pathway is a lollipop whose point size is its count; points are colored by whether the most likely next state differs from the suffix's, and those pathways are annotated with the new most likely state and its probability. The chart identifies the histories that carry information a shorter memory would lose.

The pathways are those returned by divergent_pathways(). A large divergence on a small count can be a sampling accident; check reproducibility with bootstrap_pathways(), and the pruning decision for one pathway with plot_pruning().

Usage

plot_divergence(tree, top = 15L, min_count = 5L, title = NULL, ...)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

top

Number of pathways shown. Default 15.

min_count

Pathways with a lower count are dropped. Default 5.

title

Plot title. Default NULL: a title giving the number of pathways.

...

Ignored.

Value

A ggplot object: one lollipop per pathway, divergence (bits) on the x-axis.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) tree is not a transitiontrees object.

transitiontrees_empty_result

(error) no pathway reaches min_count.

See also

divergent_pathways() for the table; plot_pathways(), plot_pruning(), bootstrap_pathways().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
plot_divergence(tree, top = 10)
